intro: On TikTok, people decide in a moment whether to watch or swipe, so your product needs to show up right away and look like it belongs in the feed. AIVideosUGC turns one product photo and a short description into a vertical video ad of 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. You might describe a hand lifting the product off a desk, a bottle on a gym bench, or a phone case catching the light, and the clip is built around that moment. For a trend or challenge, show one repeatable move; for spoken audio, keep the frame hands-only and add your narration after download; a creator version can use a face-to-camera explanation.

It suits sellers trying their first TikTok ad and marketers who need a new angle every week without booking a shoot. Each video is made one at a time, with the credit cost shown before you start. Want a different opening? Run another version. Once you download the file, add captions, a sound and your offer in TikTok or CapCut, then upload it to TikTok Ads Manager.

tips: Keep the product clear of the right edge and the bottom of the frame, where TikTok's buttons and caption sit.
To compare a new opening, make another version and change only the first scene; use Ads Manager to compare the results.

faq.q: Can I send the video straight to TikTok from AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: No. Download the file, then upload it in TikTok Ads Manager or the TikTok app. That's also where you can add captions and pick a sound.

faq.q: How long can a TikTok In-Feed ad run?
faq.a: Non-Spark In-Feed ads can run up to 10 minutes. AIVideosUGC makes 6, 10, 15 or 30-second clips, so check the format requirements and preview your creative before publishing.

faq.q: Does the video come with music?
faq.a: We don't add music, so choose a sound in TikTok or CapCut before you post.

faq.q: Do I need to label an AI-generated ad on TikTok?
faq.a: TikTok’s AI-content labeling control can vary by creative and market. Apply the in-app label when Ads Manager marks it as required.

faq.q: What product photo works best for a TikTok ad?
faq.a: Use a clear photo that shows the whole item and the part that will move, then describe one action and leave room around the edges for TikTok controls.

faq.q: Where do I add captions, prices and offers?
faq.a: Add exact wording, prices and offers in TikTok, CapCut or another editor after download; the generated clip does not contain your final text or sound.

faq.q: Do I need a model or a creator to make these?
faq.a: No. The clip is generated from your product photo and a one-sentence description, so there is no creator to book or film. Add your own caption and sound after download.

faq.q: Is this different from hiring a UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. A hired creator films their own footage and sends it to you days later; AIVideosUGC builds the clip from your own product photo on demand, and you can run a second version whenever the angle stops working.

overview.h2: Build the first TikTok beat around the product
overview.d: Start with one product action that reads without an explanation: a lid opening, a zipper closing, a brush clearing crumbs, or a bottle placed beside a sink. Upload the clearest photo you own, name the setting and movement in one sentence, and keep the product in view before the action begins.

overview.h2: Match the file to the placement
overview.d: TikTok's official In-Feed guide lists a 9:16 vertical file at a minimum 540×960, plus 1:1 at 640×640 and 16:9 at 960×540. Non-Spark In-Feed uploads can be up to 10 minutes and 500 MB. AIVideosUGC offers five video shapes—9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4—and 6, 10, 15 or 30 second jobs; those are our generator options, not TikTok upload limits. Keep key details clear of the interface and use the preview before publishing. The safe zone changes with the video shape, caption length and add-ons; choose the matching file in [TikTok's In-Feed ad specs](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/tiktok-auction-in-feed-ads) and preview before publishing.

overview.h2: Write a hook that earns the first swipe
overview.d: Put the product and the start of its action in the opening beat. A creator can lift a bottle beside their face, a hand can open a cable organizer, or a shoe can turn to reveal its tread. Describe one change only, keep the item fully inside the vertical crop, and finish with a still frame that lets the viewer recognize it before the interface overlays cover the bottom.

overview.h2: Separate In-Feed creative from Spark post
overview.d: Use a non-Spark In-Feed upload when you are supplying the asset directly to an ad. Spark Ads use an existing TikTok post and account permissions, so prepare the post and authorization in TikTok rather than assuming a downloaded file becomes a Spark ad. In either case, check current upload requirements, safe zone, captions, and sound in Ads Manager before launch.

overview.h2: Make the product readable with audio off
overview.d: A viewer may see the first seconds with audio muted. Show the hand, product, and outcome clearly enough that the action makes sense with the audio off, then add a concise caption in TikTok or CapCut. Avoid baking prices or claims into the generated frame; put exact offers in editable caption and headline fields where you can correct them.

overview.h2: Choose a TikTok scene by job
overview.d: Use a trend-challenge frame when you want a repeatable move, a hands-only setup when you will record spoken audio later, or a creator frame when the seller should explain one feature to camera. These are visual starting points; add spoken audio, captions and sound in TikTok or CapCut after download.

input_guide.h2: Prepare one photo for a readable first frame

items.d: Include the parts that will move or be handled, such as a bottle cap, shoe laces, or a bag strap. A missing edge gives the scene less to work with.
Describe one handoff, pour, open, turn, or use. A single action is easier to judge than a list of unrelated movements.
Compose the source so the product can sit away from the lower and side edges. Add exact captions later, after seeing where TikTok places buttons and text.
